correctness.rationale: The previously known domination minimum 2(k+1) comes from k+1 disjoint Kneser vertices. The inspected proof counts k-set hitting witnesses to exclude label-2 family sizes 0..k and weights beyond k+1, then uses the Roman domination property to force disjointness at equality. Exactly (k+1) disjoint blocks plus s unused elements yields the quotient factorial vertex count, and replacement by a k-block from the unused set gives degree (k+1)binom(s,k). For s<k no move exists; for s=k each state belongs to an immutable partition of n into k+2 k-blocks, with all choices of unused block adjacent. For s>=k+1, occupied/free element swaps connect token-jump configurations, and an auxiliary KG(n-k^2,k) on >=2k+1 available elements implements exchanges as genuine disjoint slides. Exhaustive k=2 state graph checks n=6..9 give 15,105,105,1 components respectively. The infinite theorem follows from exchange connectivity and the constructive Kneser path lemma, not the finite enumeration.

This classification is not merely recomputing the old minimum weight; the new object is the entire graph of optimum labelings.

value.rationale: Reconfiguration mobility is a natural independent structural question after characterizing optimal Roman labelings. The theorem gives the first nonzero-mobility point, complete partition-clique critical layer, exact connectedness threshold and degree for the entire natural integer family. This is a meaningful phase transition, not an arbitrary tiny census.

final_claim: For K(n,k), integers k>=2,n>=k(k+1), all minimum total Roman dominating functions label 2 on exactly k+1 disjoint k-subsets. Their disjoint-Kneser-adjacent one-token sliding graph has N=n!/[s!(k!)^(k+1)(k+1)!] states and degree (k+1)C(s,k), with isolates for s<k, cliques K_{k+2} for s=k, and one connected component for s>=k+1, s=n-k(k+1).
